steps: Weigh one batch: 26 lb Mulcoa 70 calcined mullite grog (Clay Art Center's "CE70"), 15 lb Greenstripe fireclay, 4 lb Raw kyanite (Virginia Kyanite), 5 lb Dextrin, and 12 lb of water (24.0 % of the dry mix). 18 batches cover the lining with 10 % to spare.
Mix the dry ingredients first, then add the water and mix to an even paste.
Fold in foam until the mix is 55 % of the cast volume air: a level US quart of it then weighs 1.86 lb (845 g). Weigh a quart from each batch and add foam or mix to correct it.
Cast it, and from the same batch cast test pieces to fire and measure.
Nothing in this mix sets with water: it holds only by drying, and stays weak until it is fired. Keep it dry, and support it until then.
Dry it out and fire it on the schedule below.
Fire test pieces to the kiln's top temperature, measure their fired density and shrinkage, and enter them under measured: they replace the estimates here.

steps: Weigh one batch: 15 lb Mulcoa 70 calcined mullite grog (Clay Art Center's "CE70"), 25 lb Greenstripe fireclay, 5 lb Raw kyanite (Virginia Kyanite), 5 lb Dextrin, 0.25 lb Newspaper pulp, and 14.5 lb of water (28.9 % of the dry mix). 71 batches cover the lining with 10 % to spare.
Mix the dry ingredients first, then add the water and mix to an even paste.
Fold in foam until the mix is 60 % of the cast volume air: a level US quart of it then weighs 1.58 lb (718 g). Weigh a quart from each batch and add foam or mix to correct it.
Cast it, and from the same batch cast test pieces to fire and measure.
Nothing in this mix sets with water: it holds only by drying, and stays weak until it is fired. Keep it dry, and support it until then.
Dry it out and fire it on the schedule below.
Fire test pieces to the kiln's top temperature, measure their fired density and shrinkage, and enter them under measured: they replace the estimates here.

findings.message: Gas piping, regulators, safety valves and the installation must be done or checked by a licensed gas fitter to your local code (NFPA 54 and 58 in the US).
Weld the frame and fit it before the arch form comes out: the steel is what holds the arch up.
The front wall is the door: bricked up, dry, for each firing. Lay the inner and outer courses together, staggered, with a header course two-thirds of the way up.
Side-mounted burners need a bag wall so the flames don't hit the ware: hard brick, first course solid in front of the burners.
Damper: a kiln shelf in a slot 12 in wide and one course high, about a foot above the top of the flue. Brace the chimney with angle at its corners and tie it to the kiln frame.

Three spy holes, 2¼ × 2½ in (a quarter brick), in the door: about 8 in above the floor (a course above any burner ports there), midway and near the top, a few inches off centre so they miss the shelf posts. Cone packs in the top and bottom, draw rings in the middle.

working.note: Build it this size and brick it down to tune the kiln: it is much easier to restrict than to enlarge (p.151, p.236). Size the damper to close it fully.

working.note: With burners under gas pressure (or a blower) the gas drives the flow; the chimney and stack only need to carry the gases out above where people are.

findings.message: Foamed fireclay backup with paper fibre (the notes' "K16 type") runs down to 130.6 °F (data from 500 °F); past its data sheet's points the conductivity is carried on along the nearest pair of points above the data, and held at the first point's value below it (no lower: more heat loss, the safe side).
findings.reference: your mix; conductivity from its fired density (castables.md §6.3)

findings.message: The skewbacks and the fill beside the arch are drawn along the arch's radius at the springline and counted by volume. The skewback's face must match the arch: 66° to the horizontal here, 90° less half the arch's central angle (HarbisonWalker's 60° skews suit a 60° arch, its 48° skews one at 2.302 in/ft). The steel that takes the arch's thrust is in the frame.
